small_guidance:
- The conv now likely dominates runtime (fast_p=0.96, baseline=3.19ms). Further tuning of the LSE/groupnorm tail won't help much; but you can still try larger BLOCK_S (8192/16384) with num_warps=8/16 in `fused_lse_kernel` since the per-program work is `C * BLOCK_S` and C=64 is small — fewer programs may reduce launch overhead.
- Merge `affine_params_kernel` into the start of `fused_lse_kernel` (load mean/invstd/gamma/beta once per program at the top, compute a/b in registers) to eliminate one launch and the N×C scratch buffers.
- In `groupnorm_stats_kernel`, swap loop order (outer over s_start, inner static over channels) and use a single contiguous load over the group's CPG*S elements when CPG*S is small enough; current double loop with BLOCK_S vector accumulators wastes registers.
large_guidance:
- Replace `nn.Conv2d` with a custom Triton im2col-style GEMM kernel: in_channels=8, kernel=3 → K=72, OC=64, output spatial=126×126. K is tiny so a direct conv (one program per (N, OC_tile, OH_tile, OW_tile), accumulating over IC×kh×kw inline) will be much faster than cuDNN for this shape and will expose fusion with the downstream pipeline.
- Fuse the entire pipeline end-to-end into two kernels: (1) custom conv producing `x_conv` in channels_last layout, (2) a single persistent kernel per (N, spatial-tile) that streams channels twice — first pass computes group mean/var (Welford or two-pass), second pass computes normalized→tanh→hardswish→add residual→online-LSE — without ever materializing N×C scratch buffers. With C=64 and S=126², a row of 64 channels fits easily in registers/SMEM, so a persistent per-(N, spatial-tile) design avoids the current 3-launch sequence.
- Alternatively keep conv as torch but write one mega-kernel that takes `x_conv` plus gn weight/bias and produces LSE directly: per (N, spatial-block) program, load all C values for the block into SMEM, compute per-group stats by reduction across the channel-group axis within the program, then do the epilogue+LSE in-place. This eliminates the stats→affine→lse round-trip through global memory.
